\label{euler_lagrangian_for_L}
Let $s \geqslant 1$ and $p \in [0, s]$. Then, the solution $u^*$ to heat equation in $(\ref{eq:heat_pde})$ is the minimizer of the total loss function $L_{\epsilon,\beta}(u)$ over $\mathcal{U}_0 := H^{p}_{t}(0,T;H_{x}^{2s+2-2p}(\Omega)) \cap L^{2}_{t}(0,T;H^{1}_{0,x}(\Omega)) \cap \{u : \Omega \times [0,T] \to \mathbb{R} | u(x,0)=u^{*}_{0}(x)\}$, i.e., $u^* = \arg\min_{u \in \mathcal{U}_0} L_{\epsilon,\beta}(u)$ for any $\epsilon, \beta > 0$.

\cite{pmlr-v134-lu21a} proved the slow generalization error using a one-layer neural network with $m$ neurons for elliptic PDEs, and \cite{lustatistical} improved this bound to fast generalization error with $J$-truncated Fourier series instead. Their generalization bounds also suffer

Let $L=\triangle$ and $\alpha>0$. $u$ satisfies the scaling invariant property such that $u(\frac{x}{\alpha}, \frac{t}{\alpha^{2}})$ is a solution to the PDE problem (\ref{linear_parabolic_pdes}) if and only if $u(x,t)$ is a solution to the PDE problem (\ref{linear_parabolic_pdes}).

title: Proof

This proof follows directly from the fact that $w(\frac{x}{\alpha}, \frac{t}{\alpha^{2}})$  and $v(\frac{x}{\alpha}, \frac{t}{\alpha^{2}})$ solves $u_{t}-\triangle u =0$ if and only if $w(x,t)$ and $v(x,t)$ solves  $u_{t}-\triangle u =0$.
Therefore, it is immediately followed by direct computation that $u(x,t)$ also enjoys this scaling invariance property.

label: prop:parabolic-balance
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Sampling Balance

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Lower bound on the temporal sample size.}
We first show lower bound on temporal sample complexity $n$. Given temporal samples $t_1,\dots,t_n$, it is enough to look at the evaluation map $ev:\ u\in V_{J,J^{2}}\;\longmapsto\;
\big(\partial_t^kD_x^\alpha u(X_{ij},t_j)\big)_{i\leqslant m,\
j\leqslant n}$. It is clear the evaluation mapping $ev$ is linear on the finite-dimensional space $V_{J,J^2}$, so it fails to be injective if its kernel is nontrivial.We will show  the contrapositive is true.

We choose $\psi=\sum_{\tau=1}^{K}c_\tau\phi_\tau\in\Psi_K$ with
its coefficient vector $c\in\mathbb{R}^K$, with $
\psi^{(k)}(t_j)=0$ and $\psi(0)=0$, for $1\leqslant j\leqslant n, 0\leqslant k\leqslant r$. It forms a homogeneous linear system $Ac=0$ with evaluation matrix
\[
A=
\begin{pmatrix}
\phi_1(t_1) & \phi_2(t_1) & \cdots & \phi_K(t_1)\\
\phi_1'(t_1) & \phi_2'(t_1) & \cdots & \phi_K'(t_1)\\
\vdots & \vdots & & \vdots\\
\phi_1(t_n) & \phi_2(t_n) & \cdots & \phi_K(t_n)\\
\phi_1'(t_n) & \phi_2'(t_n) & \cdots & \phi_K'(t_n)\\
\phi_1(0) & \phi_2(0) & \cdots & \phi_K(0)
\end{pmatrix}
\in\mathbb{R}^{\big(2n+1\big)\times K}
\]. The matrix has $2n+1$ rows, so
$\text{rank} A\leqslant 2n+1<K$, and the rank--nullity theorem gives
\[
\dim\ker A\;=\;K-\text{rank} A\;\geqslant\;K-2n-1\;\geqslant\;1
\]
The corresponding
$\psi\in\Psi_K\setminus\{0\}$ vanishes, together with its first $r$
derivatives, at every temporal position $t_{j}$. Pick any spatial basis element
$\phi_\xi$ with $|\xi|_\infty\leqslant J$ and set
$v:=\psi\,\phi_\xi\in V_{J,J^2}\setminus\{0\}$; by the tensor structure,
for all $0\leqslant k\leqslant r$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^d$,
\[
\partial_t^kD_x^\alpha v\,(X_{ij},t_j)
=\psi^{(k)}(t_j)\,D_x^\alpha\phi_\xi(X_{ij})=0 ,
\]
so $v\in\ker\mathrm{ev}$ and $\mathrm{ev}$ is not injective. Since
$K\asymp J^2$, \eqref{eq:n-lower} follows.

Next, we show upper bound on the spatial sample size $m$.
Using $n\geqslant J^2$, we fix
$\phi_\tau$ at the temporal level $2^\ell\asymp J^2$ and $\phi_\xi$
with $|\xi|_\infty\leqslant J$, $supp\,\phi_\xi\subset\Omega^\circ$, and
consider the squared basis direction
$h_J:=a_J^2\phi_\xi^2\phi_\tau^2$ in the loss class, with admissible
amplitude $a_J$. We deonote $P_X$, $P_T$ for the uniform laws on $\Omega$
and $[0,T]$, and $\widehat P$, $P$ as the empirical and population
means on $\Omega_T$, decompose
\begin{align}
&(\widehat P-P)h_J=W_J+B_J,\\
&W_J:=\frac1n\sum_{j=1}^n\Big[\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m h_J(X_{ij},t_j)
-P_Xh_J(\cdot,t_j)\Big],\\
&B_J:=\frac1n\sum_{j=1}^nP_Xh_J(\cdot,t_j)-Ph_J.
\end{align}

Define the events
\[
E_1:=\Big\{|B_J|\geqslant c_1a_J^2\sqrt{J^2/n}\Big\},
\qquad
E_2:=\Big\{|W_J|<\tfrac{c_1}{2}\,a_J^2\sqrt{J^2/n}\Big\}.
\]
By lemma \ref{lem:moments_of_wavelets}, 
\[
\mathbb{E} W_J^2
\lesssim\;a_J^4\,\frac{J^{d+2}}{nm}, \quad\quad \mathbb{P}(E_1)\geqslant c_2
\]
using $\int\phi_\xi^4\asymp J^d$ and $\int\phi_\tau^4\asymp J^2$ and
Chebyshev's inequality,
\[
\mathbb{P}(E_2^c)
\;\leqslant\;\frac{4\,\mathbb{E} W_J^2}{c_1^2\,a_J^4\,J^2/n}
\;\lesssim\;\frac{J^d}{m}
\;\leqslant\;\frac{c_2}{2}
\qquad\text{once } m\geqslant C_0J^d
\]
for a sufficiently large constant $C_0(c_{1},c_{2})$. Hence
\[
\mathbb{P}(E_1\cap E_2)\;\geqslant\;\mathbb{P}(E_1)-\mathbb{P}(E_2^c)
\;\geqslant\;c_2-\frac{c_2}{2}\;=\;\frac{c_2}{2},
\]
and on $E_1\cap E_2$ the reverse triangle inequality gives
\[
\big|(\widehat P-P)h_J\big|
\;=\;|B_J+W_J|
\;\geqslant\;|B_J|-|W_J|
\;>\;c_1a_J^2\sqrt{J^2/n}-\tfrac{c_1}{2}\,a_J^2\sqrt{J^2/n}
\;=\;\tfrac{c_1}{2}\,a_J^2\sqrt{J^2/n}\,.
\]

The direction $h_J$ lies in the localized fixed-$J$ class over which our inequality bounds the empirical process by
$C\,a_J^2\sqrt{J^{d+2}\log(1+C_2N)/N}$ if 
\[
\sqrt{\frac{J^2}{n}}\;\lesssim\;\sqrt{\frac{J^{d+2}\log(1+C_2nm)}{nm}},
\qquad
\]
This implies $
m\;\lesssim\;J^{d}\log(1+C_2nm)$, and furthermore  $n\;\gtrsim\;J^2\;\gtrsim\;\Big(\frac{m}{\log(1+C_2nm)}\Big)^{2/d},
$

label: lem:morrey_embedding
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:morrey_embedding}
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded domain
with $C^1$ boundary. Let $1\le p<\infty$ and
$k,m\in\mathbb N_0$ satisfy $m>d/p$.
Then the embedding
\[
W^{k+m,p}(\Omega)\hookrightarrow C^k(\overline\Omega)
\]
is continuous and compact. Then
\begin{equation}
W^{k+m,p} \hookrightarrow C^{k}(\bar{\Omega}).
\end{equation}
In particular, the embedding is compact if $m-\frac{d}{p}>k$.
\label{Sobolev_embedding}

label: lemma_F.8

body_md:
\label{lemma_F.8} Given $p,q\geqslant 0$. Assume $f\in H^{p}_{t}(\mathbb{R};H^{q}_{x}(\mathbb{R}^{d}))\cap \mathcal{F}_{J,J}$ and $f$ admits spatial-temporal Fourier series with smooth basis dense in $L^{2}$ on compact space-time domain $\Omega_{T} = \Omega\times [0,T]$, then the following estimates hold \\
\begin{align}
||P_{J}f||_{L^{2}_{t}(\mathbb{R};L^{2}_{x}(\mathbb{R}^{d}))}^{2} &\leqslant C(\Omega,T)||f||_{H^{1}_{t}([0,T];H^{1}_{x}(\Omega))}^{2}, \\
||P_{J}f||_{\infty}&\leqslant C(\Omega)R, \hspace{1.7cm}\text{if }\,\, q>\frac{d}{2},\\
||P_{J}f||_{\infty}&\leqslant C(\Omega,T)J^{d+2}, \hspace{0.8cm}\text{if }\,\, q\leqslant\frac{d}{2},
\end{align}
where $C_{1}(\Omega, T)$ is a constant depending on $\Omega_{T}$
\label{J_truncation_estimates}.

title: Proof
body_md:
By the change of variables $u=2^\ell t-k_0$,
$\int\phi_\tau^{2q}=2^{\ell(q-1)}\|\varphi\|_{L^{2q}}^{2q}$ for
$q\in\{1,2,4\}$, whence $\mathbb{E} Y_1=T^{-1}$,
$\mathbb{E} Y_1^2\asymp2^\ell\asymp J^2$, and
$\mathbb{E} Y_1^4\asymp2^{3\ell}\asymp J^6$; \eqref{eq:moments} follows. For
i.i.d.\ centered variables,
\[
\mathbb{E} B^2=\frac{\text{Var}(Y_1)}{n},
\qquad
\mathbb{E} B^4=\frac{\mathbb{E}(Y_1-\mathbb{E} Y_1)^4}{n^3}
+\frac{3(n-1)}{n^3}\text{Var}(Y_1)^2
\lesssim\frac{J^6}{n^3}+\frac{J^4}{n^2}.
\]
If $n\geqslant J^2$, then $J^6/n^3\leqslant J^4/n^2$, so
$\mathbb{E} B^4\leqslant\kappa\,(\mathbb{E} B^2)^2$ for an absolute constant
$\kappa$. The Paley--Zygmund inequality applied to $B^2$ gives, for
$\theta\in(0,1)$,
\[
\mathbb{P}\big(B^2\geqslant\theta\,\mathbb{E} B^2\big)
\geqslant(1-\theta)^2\frac{(\mathbb{E} B^2)^2}{\mathbb{E} B^4}
\geqslant\frac{(1-\theta)^2}{\kappa};
\]
taking $\theta=\tfrac12$ and using $\mathbb{E} B^2\asymp J^2/n$ yields
\eqref{eq:anticonc}.
